rule: The arrowhead turns 90° clockwise at each cell in reading order (up, right, down, left, …). Row 3 is down, left, so the missing cell is up. Columns agree: each turns 90° counter-clockwise per row.
shortcut: none

rule: The T's stem turns 45° clockwise per column within each row: E,SE,S / SE,S,SW / NE,E,? gives SE. Columns also agree (+45° then -90°).
shortcut: none

rule: Distribution of three for count (1/2/3) and for fill (black/dotted/white), across rows and columns. The missing cell is 2 dotted diamonds.
shortcut: Novelty: the three distractors are exact copies of matrix cells (opt1=r1c2, opt2=r2c3, opt4=r1c1), so the answer is the only option not already shown.
legibility: Dots inside the matrix diamonds are about 20 px, roughly 6 dp on the phone. Readable but small.

rule: The dot moves 90° clockwise around the square frame per column (8 positions, 2 steps each): BR,BL,TL / L,T,R / R,B,? gives L (middle of the left side). Columns are also consistent (+135° then +180°).
shortcut: none

rule: The dot moves 90° counter-clockwise per column among the 4 diagonal positions: SE,NE,NW / NE,NW,SW / SW,SE,? gives NE. Columns are also consistent (90° counter-clockwise, then 180°).
shortcut: none

rule: Outer shape (square/hexagon/circle) and inner symbol (triangle/cross/star) each appear once per row and once per column. The missing cell is a hexagon with a triangle.
shortcut: Novelty: the distractors are copies of matrix cells (opt1=r1c2, opt2=r3c1, opt4=r2c2), so the answer is the only option not already shown.

rule: Line segments: col3 = col1 XOR col2 (lines in both cancel out). Row 3: {both diagonals + bottom} XOR {left, bottom, / diagonal} = left + \ diagonal.
shortcut: none (AND/intersection would give opt1, but AND fails rows 1 and 2)

rule: col3 = union (OR) of the segments in col1 and col2. Row 3: {top, left, /} ∪ {top, left, bottom} = top + left + bottom + / diagonal. XOR fails row 1.
shortcut: none

rule: Dot positions in the die: col3 = col1 XOR col2. Row 3: {TL,C,BL,BR} XOR {TR,BL,BR} = {TL,TR,C}. Union fails row 1.
shortcut: none

rule: col3 = union of the dot positions in col1 and col2. Row 3: {C,BL} ∪ {C,TR} = {TR,C,BL}. XOR fails row 1.
shortcut: none

rule: Count follows the column (1,2,3). Shape (diamond/triangle/square) appears once per row and once per column. The missing cell is 3 diamonds.
shortcut: Novelty: the distractors are copies of matrix cells (opt2=r1c3, opt3=r3c2, opt4=r2c2).

rule: Count follows the row (1,2,3). Fill (white/dotted/black) appears once per row and once per column. The missing cell is 3 dotted triangles.
shortcut: Novelty: the distractors are copies of matrix cells (opt1=r3c1, opt2=r2c2, opt4=r2c1).
legibility: Dot inside the matrix triangles is about 20 px (6 dp) in a triangle about 20 dp wide, with about 2 dp between dot and outline. Readable, but this is the finest detail in the set.

rule: Shape (hexagon/square/diamond) and fill (hatched/white/black) each appear once per row and once per column. The missing cell is a hatched square.
shortcut: Novelty: the distractors are copies of matrix cells (opt1=r2c1, opt2=r1c1, opt4=r3c2).
legibility: Hatching is about 1.8 dp lines with about 2.6 dp gaps in matrix shapes about 25 dp wide. It reads as a grey texture but stays distinct from white and black. Minor hatch-clipping blobs thicken the outline at the hexagon corners (r1c1 and option 2) and at the diamond tip (r2c2).

rule: Direction is constant within each row (NW, NE, SE). Count follows the column (1,2,3). The missing cell is 3 SE arrows.
shortcut: Novelty: the distractors are copies of matrix cells (opt2=r2c2, opt3=r2c3, opt4=r3c2).

rule: Count follows the column (1,2,3). Fill (white/dotted/black) appears once per row and once per column. The missing cell is 3 white circles.
shortcut: Novelty: the distractors are copies of matrix cells (opt1=r1c2, opt2=r2c3, opt3=r2c2).

rule: Count is always 2. Shape (diamond/square/triangle) and fill (dotted/white/black) each appear once per row and once per column. The missing cell is 2 white diamonds.
shortcut: Novelty: the distractors are copies of matrix cells (opt1=r2c2, opt3=r1c3, opt4=r2c1).

rule: The arrowhead's tip (the vertex opposite the notch) turns 90° clockwise per column: S,W,N / NW,NE,SE / SE,SW,? gives NW. Columns are also consistent (+135° then +180°). Fill (hatched/black/white) appears once per row and column, so the answer is hatched.
shortcut: none
legibility: Rotated darts are perceptually ambiguous because the wing tips (about 34°) are sharper than the tip (about 48°). The black SE darts in r2c3 and r3c1 can read as 'pointing up'. The hatched dart in r1c1 is about 23 dp and shows only about 4 hatch strokes.

rule: Shape (pacman/dart/T) appears once per row and column. All three shapes in a row share one orientation (pacman mouth, dart tip, T bar), which turns 90° clockwise per row: NW, NE, SE. The missing cell is a dart pointing SE.
shortcut: Novelty: the distractors are copies of matrix cells (opt1=r2c3, opt2=r2c1, opt4=r3c2).

rule: Outer shape (hexagon/square/circle) appears once per row and column, so the missing one is a square. Dots: col3 = col1 XOR col2, so row 3 is {C,BL} XOR {TR,C,BL,BR} = {TR,BR}.
shortcut: none

rule: Outer shape (circle/square/diamond) appears once per row and column, so the missing one is a circle. The dot moves 90° clockwise per column (B,L,T / T,R,B / L,T,?), so it sits on the right. Columns are consistent (+180° then -90°).
shortcut: none (the answer is a copy of r2c2, so the novelty heuristic would mislead here)

rule: Count follows the column (1,2,3). Direction turns 90° counter-clockwise per column: NE,NW,SW / SW,SE,NE / SE,NE,? gives NW. Columns are consistent (+180° then -90°).
shortcut: Novelty: the distractors are copies of matrix cells (opt1=r1c2, opt2=r3c2, opt3=r2c3).

rule: Shape (dart/pacman/T) and fill (hatched/black/white) each appear once per row and column, so the answer is a black dart. Orientation (dart tip, pacman mouth, T bar side) turns 90° clockwise per column: W,N,E / NE,SE,SW / SW,NW,? gives NE. Columns are also consistent (+135° then +180°). Reading the T by its stem instead of its bar gives a different self-consistent pattern (c1=c3 in each row, r2=r3 in each column) that predicts SW, which no option offers, so the solver has to fall back to the bar reading.
shortcut: none
legibility: The hatched T in r3c2 has bars about 9 dp wide, where the 45° hatch looks like ladder rungs. The rotated darts are perceptually ambiguous (same issue as g17). Options 2 and 4 differ only in the dart's rotation.

rule: Outer shape (hexagon/circle/square) appears once per row and column, so the missing one is a circle. Dots: col3 = col1 ∪ col2, so row 3 is {TR,BL} ∪ {C,BL} = {TR,C,BL}. XOR fails row 1.
shortcut: none

rule: Fill (black/white/hatched) appears once per row and column, so the answer is white. The T's bar side turns 45° clockwise per column: E,SE,S / NW,N,NE / W,NW,? gives N (upright T). Columns are consistent (-135° then -45°).
shortcut: none
legibility: Hatched T bars are about 9 dp wide with 1.8 dp hatch lines. Fine, though the diagonal Ts need careful bar-vs-stem parsing.
